*   Island

That's 3 lands, which is generally a good starting point for a 7-card hand. Spinerock Knoll is interesting, it's a land that comes into play tapped unless you control two or more other lands, which we don't right now, so it will enter tapped. Swiftwater Cliffs is a tap land, entering tapped and giving us a life. These tap lands slow us down a bit, but still provide mana.

**Spells:**
*   Awaken the Sky Tyrant (3R) - Creates a 4/4 Dragon
*   Mystic Retrieval (3U) - Recurses a spell from the graveyard to hand, then flashback for 1UR.
*   Dragon Mage (5RR) - 5/5 Dragon flier. When it deals combat damage to a player, each player discards their hand and draws 7 cards.
*   Psychosis Crawler (5 Colorless) - Generic 0/0 that gets +1/+1 for each card in your hand, and when you draw a card, each opponent loses 1 life.

**Evaluation:**
This hand has good mana colors (blue and red) to cast our spells. However, the spells themselves are quite expensive. Awaken the Sky Tyrant is 4 mana, Mystic Retrieval is 4 mana, and Dragon Mage and Psychosis Crawler are 7 and 5 mana respectively.

With our current lands, we can play a tapped land turn 1, a basic Island turn 2, and then theoretically have 3 mana on turn 3 if Spinerock Knoll comes in untapped. But it won't, so we'll have 2 untapped lands by turn 3. This means our first spell would be Awaken the Sky Tyrant on turn 4, assuming we draw another land.

The problem is the high mana costs of our action spells. Psychosis Crawler is a 5-drop, Dragon Mage is a 7-drop. Even with 3 lands, we're going to be waiting a while to cast anything significant. Mystic Retrieval is also a late-game card that relies on having something in the graveyard already.

Given that we are the starting player and aiming for optimal play, we need to apply pressure early or set up our board quickly. This hand offers neither. It's too slow and clunky. While it has lands, the curve is way too high.

Therefore, for competitive play, this is a clear mulligan. We want to find a hand with a lower curve or more early interaction to stay ahead.

I'm going to choose to mulligan.

annotations.description: The player is putting Forest on the bottom of their library, but Forest is their only green source alongside Haven of the Spirit Dragon (which only adds colored mana for Dragon creature spells). Looking at their hand, they have Commander's Sphere (3 mana), Dragon's Hoard (3 mana), Bag of Tricks (needs green), Rishkar's Expertise (needs double green), and Skyship Stalker (needs double red). With Vrondiss as their commander (costs 3RG), they desperately need green mana. Forest is one of the most critical cards in this hand as a basic land that produces green. Rishkar's Expertise is a 6-mana spell that requires double green and creatures with power to be effective - it's the most cuttable card in this opening hand since it won't be castable for many turns and requires board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Forest on the bottom of their library
annotations.betterLine: Put Rishkar's Expertise on the bottom - it's a 6-mana spell requiring board presence and double green, making it the worst keep in an opening hand that already has mana concerns. Forest is essential as a green source for casting Vrondiss and activating Bag of Tricks.

annotations.description: In the mulligan/bottom decision for a 6-card hand (after mulligan to 6), the player needs to put one card on the bottom. The hand has only one land (Mountain) plus Bojuka Bog (enters tapped), with Rakdos Signet and Mind Stone as 2-mana rocks. Keeping both 2-mana rocks is important for acceleration, but Unstable Obelisk at 3 mana is also a ramp piece and removal. However, the real concern is that Hex at 6 mana is very expensive and requires exactly 6 target creatures to be legal - it's often a dead card. Bottoming Hex instead of Unstable Obelisk would preserve more versatility, as Unstable Obelisk provides both ramp and permanent removal. That said, Unstable Obelisk is slow and the hand already has two cheaper rocks, so this is debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed Unstable Obelisk, keeping Bojuka Bog, Mountain, Hex, Mind Stone, Rakdos Signet
annotations.betterLine: Bottom Hex instead - it requires exactly 6 target creatures (often hard to achieve), while Unstable Obelisk provides both ramp and flexible permanent removal. The hand already has two 2-mana rocks for acceleration.

annotations.description: On turn 1, playing Forest instead of Haven of the Spirit Dragon is slightly suboptimal. The hand contains Dragon's Hoard (3 colorless), Commander's Sphere (3 colorless), and Bag of Tricks (1G). Haven of the Spirit Dragon produces colorless mana and can also produce colored mana specifically for Dragon creature spells (like Skyship Stalker). Forest only produces green. Since the player needs colorless mana for their 3-drop artifacts on turn 2-3 anyway, and Haven can serve double duty by also casting Dragons later, Haven would have been slightly better as the turn 1 land drop, saving Forest for turn 2 when green mana might be needed for Bag of Tricks.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest as their first land.
annotations.betterLine: Play Haven of the Spirit Dragon as the turn 1 land, since it produces colorless for the artifact-heavy early curve and can later help cast Dragon spells. Save Forest for turn 2 to enable Bag of Tricks activation or other green costs.

Returning Forest or Haven of the Spirit Dragon would let the Turf stay in play producing RG, and you'd replay the basic/utility land next turn untapped, netting +1 mana going forward.

annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Gray Merchant of Asphodel, dealing 2 damage to Gem25F Teach
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Gray Merchant and Florian into Gem25F Teach for 5 damage, maximizing Florian's postcombat card selection ability

annotations.description: At 12 life, KimiK2 chose to destroy Thought Vessel (a minor mana rock with no max hand size) instead of Psychosis Crawler, which deals 1 damage to each opponent per card drawn. Gem25F Teach is an Izzet deck capable of drawing many cards, making Psychosis Crawler a direct lethal threat to KimiK2 at such low life.
annotations.actionTaken: Destroyed Thought Vessel, a minor mana rock.
annotations.betterLine: Destroy Psychosis Crawler, which is an active life-draining threat that could easily kill KimiK2 at 12 life with any significant card draw from the Izzet player.

annotations.description: KimiK2 Detect tapped Haven of the Spirit Dragon for colorless mana instead of using its Dragon-specific colored mana ability. With multiple Dragon creature spells in hand (Vengeful Ancestor, Terror of Mount Velus, Taurean Mauler/Changeling), the colored mana option is strictly better when casting Dragons and could help meet color requirements, especially given the land base is heavy on Forests with limited red sources.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose option 1 ({T}: Add {C}) from Haven of the Spirit Dragon
annotations.betterLine: Choose option 2 ({T}: Add one mana of any color, spend only on Dragon creature spells) to help cast Dragon spells from hand with proper color fixing

annotations.description: At 12 life, KimiK2 chose to cast Spit Flame (a 4-damage creature removal spell) instead of deploying Hoard-Smelter Dragon, a 5/5 flyer that would significantly improve board presence. Spit Flame has graveyard recursion when a Dragon enters, so casting the Dragon first and then recovering Spit Flame later would have been strictly better sequencing. The Dragon also synergizes with Thunderbreak Regent already on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Spit Flame for creature removal
annotations.betterLine: Cast Hoard-Smelter Dragon to deploy a major flying threat alongside Thunderbreak Regent, then recover Spit Flame from graveyard later via its Dragon-trigger recursion ability

annotations.description: Attacking DSV3 Tactic who is at 69 life with a 3/3 Beast Token is nearly irrelevant. Two other opponents (Gem25F Teach at 13hp, KimiK2 Detect at 12hp) are at critically low life totals where 3 damage is significant and brings them closer to lethal range.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked DSV3 Tactic (69 life) with a 3/3 Beast Token for trivial damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack Gem25F Teach (13 life, no blockers) or KimiK2 Detect (12 life, Thunderbreak Regent can't block ground) to apply meaningful pressure on a near-death opponent.

annotations.description: GPT5n ESPN chose 'Break Their Chains' (destroy target artifact) mode on You Find Some Prisoners, but looking at the board, the only notable artifacts on opponents' boards are Worn Powerstone (Gem25F Teach) and Outpost Siege is an enchantment, not an artifact. While destroying Worn Powerstone is fine, the 'Interrogate Them' mode would likely be much more valuable at this stage of the game. GPT5n ESPN is at 14 life with a hand full of cards they need mana to cast (Marionette Master at 6 mana, Hex at 6 mana). Exiling top 3 cards from an opponent's library and potentially getting access to a powerful spell castable with any color of mana could provide a much-needed tempo advantage or answer. Destroying a Worn Powerstone from Gem25F Teach (who is at 13 life with an empty-looking board) is relatively low-impact compared to the potential upside of the interrogate mode, especially since Gem25F Teach doesn't appear to be the primary threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose 'Break Their Chains' mode to destroy an artifact
annotations.betterLine: Choose 'Interrogate Them' mode targeting one of the opponents (likely DSV3 Tactic at 66 life who is the biggest threat) to potentially gain access to a powerful spell, which provides more value than destroying a mana rock from a low-life opponent

annotations.description: With three opponents at 12-14 life, Theater of Horrors provides slow incremental value that won't matter if opponents stabilize or die soon. Star Athlete before combat would create immediate pressure with its menace body and attack trigger that forces opponents to either sacrifice a permanent or take 5 damage - potentially lethal range for the 12hp opponent.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Theater of Horrors (1BR) for incremental card advantage
annotations.betterLine: Play a Swamp for land drop, then cast Star Athlete (1RR) before combat to attack immediately with its powerful 5-damage attack trigger against critically low opponents. Could also cast Thought Vessel with remaining mana.

annotations.description: Attacked GPT5n ESPN who has a 3/3 Beast Token that can block and kill the 1/1 Human Soldier Token, when Gem25F Teach at 10 life has zero creatures and would take guaranteed damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked GPT5n ESPN with the 1/1 Human Soldier Token, risking it being blocked and killed by the 3/3 Beast Token.
annotations.betterLine: Attack Gem25F Teach, who has no creatures to block, guaranteeing 1 damage to the opponent at the lowest life total (10 HP).

annotations.description: Attacking GPT5n ESPN (11 life) instead of Gem25F Teach (10 life) with a 4/4 flyer. Both opponents can't block the flyer, but Gem25F Teach is at lower life and has no creatures at all, making them more vulnerable to elimination. Additionally, if KimiK2 had cast Terror of Mount Velus pre-combat (they had the mana), double strike on Thunderbreak Regent would deal 8 damage - enough to kill Gem25F Teach (10hp) but not GPT5n ESPN (11hp).
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked GPT5n ESPN with Thunderbreak Regent, dealing 4 to put them to 7 life.
annotations.betterLine: Attack Gem25F Teach to put them to 6 life, keeping open the possibility of eliminating them more easily on future turns.

annotations.description: KimiK2 attacked with only Hoard-Smelter Dragon when both flying creatures could attack unblocked against opponents at 10-11 life with no flying blockers. Attacking with both (9 total flying damage) could threaten to eliminate Gem25F Teach (10hp) or significantly pressure both low-life opponents.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Hoard-Smelter Dragon (5 damage), holding back Thunderbreak Regent
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Thunderbreak Regent and Hoard-Smelter Dragon into Gem25F Teach (10hp) for 9 damage, nearly eliminating them, or split attacks to pressure both low-life opponents. Eliminating opponents is extremely valuable in multiplayer.

annotations.description: With two opponents at 7 and 12 life, DSV3 Tactic could have played Swamp from hand (7 lands total) and cast Kaervek the Merciless (5BR = 7 mana), which would punish every spell opponents cast with damage equal to its mana value - devastating against such low life totals. Instead, they cast a 2-mana rock that provides marginal value at this stage of the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thought Vessel, a 2-mana rock providing colorless mana and no maximum hand size
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp, then cast Kaervek the Merciless (5BR) to threaten lethal damage against opponents at 7 and 12 life whenever they cast spells

annotations.description: Chose to destroy Outpost Siege over Thunderbreak Regent. KimiK2 is at 10 life - removing their 4/4 flyer would make it much easier to close the game. The 7 life cost (4 mana value + 3 Thunderbreak trigger) is trivial at 62 life. Outpost Siege provides value but KimiK2 is nearly dead anyway and has limited resources to leverage it.
annotations.actionTaken: Destroyed Outpost Siege with Feed the Swarm, losing 4 life
annotations.betterLine: Destroy Thunderbreak Regent to remove KimiK2's best creature and clear the path to finish them off at 10 life. The 7 life loss is negligible at 62 life.

annotations.description: KimiK2 Detect used Hoard-Smelter Dragon's ability to destroy their own Gruul Signet for a temporary +2/+0 buff. This permanently sacrifices a mana rock (which provides ramp in a deck that needs to cast expensive dragons like Terror of Mount Velus at 7 mana) for a marginal temporary combat buff. The reasoning about boosting Hoard-Smelter Dragon makes no sense in a non-combat context - it's the beginning of turn, and the +2/+0 only lasts until end of turn. Additionally, the prompt says 'Select an artifact' in context of Mogis, God of Slaughter being on the stack - but KimiK2 used Hoard-Smelter Dragon's activated ability to destroy their own artifact rather than targeting an opponent's artifact. There were opponent artifacts available (Worn Powerstone, Etherium-Horn Sorcerer). At 10 life with expensive cards in hand, destroying your own mana acceleration is very costly.
annotations.actionTaken: Destroyed their own Gruul Signet with Hoard-Smelter Dragon for a temporary +2/+0 buff
annotations.betterLine: Target an opponent's artifact like Worn Powerstone (Gem25F Teach's mana rock, giving +3/+0) to both deny an opponent resources and get a bigger buff, or simply not activate the ability if the temporary buff isn't needed

annotations.description: Casting Return to Nature during combat when Gem25F Teach is at 5hp and KimiK2 has 9 power of unblockable flyers (Thunderbreak Regent 4/4 + Hoard-Smelter Dragon 5/5). If the target is something on Gem25F's board (like Worn Powerstone), this is unnecessary since attacking for lethal eliminates the player entirely. The card would be better saved for a more impactful target later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Return to Nature during combat phase
annotations.betterLine: Hold Return to Nature and simply attack Gem25F Teach with either flyer for lethal damage (5hp vs 4+ flying damage). Save Return to Nature for DSV3 Tactic's Bastion of Remembrance or another high-value target later.

annotations.description: At 4 life in a 1v1 against Vial Smasher the Fierce, any spell DSV3 casts with MV 4+ will kill KimiK2 via Vial Smasher's triggered ability (which always targets KimiK2 since they're the only opponent). Casting Taurean Mauler does nothing to address this lethal threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Taurean Mauler (a 2/2 changeling) for 3 mana, ignoring the lethal Vial Smasher on DSV3's board.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Underdark Rift ({5}, {T}, exile) to tuck Vial Smasher the Fierce into DSV3's library, removing the immediate lethal threat. KimiK2 has exactly enough mana (5 from other lands + tap Rift) to activate this. Then attack with flyers to pressure DSV3's life total.

annotations.description: Chose to destroy Thought Vessel (1 mana production + no max hand size) instead of Sol Ring (2 mana production). Sol Ring is nearly always the higher-priority target as it provides double the mana acceleration. The no-maximum-hand-size upside of Thought Vessel is situational and less impactful than the extra mana Sol Ring provides every turn. The pump from Hoard-Smelter Dragon is identical either way (both MV 2).
annotations.actionTaken: Destroyed Thought Vessel with Hoard-Smelter Dragon's ability
annotations.betterLine: Destroy Sol Ring instead, removing 2 mana per turn from DSV3 Tactic's production rather than just 1 mana and a situational hand size effect

annotations.description: At 4 HP against a 59 HP opponent, KimiK2 sent Vrondiss into indestructible Mogis (7/5) where Vrondiss dies for nothing, triggers Bastion of Remembrance (losing 1 precious life), and didn't even send Thunderbreak Regent (4/4 flying) which would have added 4 unblocked damage. Every point of damage matters when trying to race down from 59.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Hoard-Smelter Dragon and Vrondiss but not Thunderbreak Regent. Vrondiss ran into indestructible Mogis and died.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures - Thunderbreak Regent and Hoard-Smelter Dragon fly over for 11 damage, and either don't send Vrondiss into the indestructible Mogis block, or accept the trade if creating the 5/4 token via enrage is worth it. At minimum, Thunderbreak Regent should have been sent.
